picks.title: Start Songs with MIDI: Suno adds MIDI file uploads as a starting point in Create
picks.rationale: Primary-source feature release: producers can seed Suno generations with their own MIDI melody, chords or arrangement, a direct change to how they steer AI songwriting.
picks.excerpt: Suno now lets users upload a MIDI file as the starting point for a generated song in Create, so producers can steer AI generation from their own melody, chords or arrangement.

picks.title: iZotope Photon is a local stem separation and denoising tool that runs off your GPU
picks.rationale: New product launch: iZotope's 12-model stem separation and cleanup tool runs locally on the GPU as an app and ARA plugin, the single Photon card for today (music owns this story).
picks.excerpt: iZotope has launched Photon, an AI-powered stem separation and audio cleanup tool powered by 12 custom-trained models that process audio locally on the computer's GPU rather than in the cloud.

picks.title: More YouTube creators can now use AI to replace copyrighted songs
picks.rationale: Feature rollout: YouTube widens access to Replace Song, which swaps Content ID-claimed music for AI-generated royalty-free instrumentals, so more creators can now clear a claim without editing the track out.
picks.excerpt: YouTube is expanding access to its AI-powered Replace Song feature, which generates royalty-free AI instrumentals to swap in for Content ID-claimed music.

picks.title: More AI Detector False Positives Emerge In Rapid Succession: Do Indie Musicians Have a Serious Problem Here?
picks.rationale: New cases of AI-music detectors flagging human recordings, including 1980s originals, as AI: a concrete risk of mislabelling and penalties for indie artists.
picks.excerpt: AI-music detectors are flagging electro-synth tracks as AI-generated - even original recordings made in the 1980s - raising the risk that indie artists get mislabelled or penalised by platforms.

picks.title: MLC Formally Opposes Udio's Streaming-Data Subpoena, Citing Two to Three Weeks of Staff Time
picks.rationale: New court filing: the MLC formally opposes Udio's subpoena for streaming data. This is a separate filing in Udio's case, not the Suno-MLC dispute we ran on 10-25.
picks.excerpt: The Mechanical Licensing Collective is pushing back on AI music company Udio's subpoena for streaming data, saying compliance would take two to three weeks of staff time.

https://www.digitalmusicnews.com/2026/11.new_action: The MLC filed a formal opposition to Udio's streaming-data subpoena (a separate filing from the Suno-MLC dispute published 10-25).
